title: coax draws ASCII stand-ins for its symbols when the config or terminal asks
body:
coax draws many characters outside ASCII and assumes the terminal's font has every one:

- the rounded message borders
- the context bar's `━` and `─`
- the fold markers `▸` and `▾`
- `COPY_GLYPH` (`⧉`) and the thought mark `✻`
- `◆`, `●` and `◐` on the status line, from `icon` in `src/header.rs`
- `↑` and `↓` on the token counts
- the circled chip numbers such as `①`
- `⋯` and the spinner
- the tool-call icons from coax-d1bcb7

When a font lacks one, the terminal draws it from a fallback font that may not fit the cell. coax-01ebbd was one such case: JetBrainsMono Nerd Font has no `▰` or `▱`. A terminal cannot tell a program which characters its font lacks.

## Proposal

- A `glyphs` key in `config.toml`, `"unicode"` or `"ascii"`. Under `"ascii"`, every character in the list above has an ASCII stand-in. The tool-call icons have theirs settled already: `=` read, `?` search, `+` edit, `x` delete, `>` move, `$` run, `v` fetch, `:` think, `~` mode, `*` agent and other.
- When the key is absent, coax uses `"ascii"` if the locale is not UTF-8 or `TERM` is `linux`, the Linux console, and `"unicode"` otherwise.

## Open

- The ASCII stand-ins for the borders, the bar, the chips and the spinner.
- Whether the `[palette]` table and `glyphs` belong under one display section of the config.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: The status line's spinner, `◐◓◑◒` in `header::SPINNER`, is missing from JetBrainsMono Nerd Font, so ghostty draws it from a fallback font, like the old `▰▱` bar. The picker's new spinner is braille and is in the font. Its glyphs sit together in constants at the top of `src/picker.rs`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: Jack decided: under `glyphs = "ascii"` the rounded message borders become `+`, `-` and `|` boxes. He left the other stand-ins to the implementer.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text:
Landed uncommitted in the tree. `src/glyphs.rs` holds a `Glyphs` enum, `Unicode` or `Ascii`, set once at startup like the palette: `glyphs::init` takes `detect(config.glyphs, env)`, and `glyphs::get` reads it. The config's `glyphs` key wins. Without it, coax looks at the first non-empty of `LC_ALL`, `LC_CTYPE` and `LANG`, and draws ASCII unless that names UTF-8 or utf8. `TERM=linux` draws ASCII in any locale. A raw agent command reads no config, so only the environment decides there.

Rather than a second glyph set threaded through every drawing function, `glyphs::fold` rewrites each finished frame's cells through one table, `glyphs::stand_in`, just before the terminal shows it. That one pass covers coax's own symbols, ratatui's rounded borders and cmr's markdown, which draws `─ │ ┼ • ┌ … ┆ ▪`. Every stand-in is one column, so no width math changes. The chips stay `①` to `⑳` in the prompt's text and in what is sent, and only their cells are drawn as `1` to `9`, then `A` to `K`. Text an agent sends that holds one of the table's characters is drawn folded too.

| stand-in | characters |
|---|---|
| `+` | `╭ ╮ ╰ ╯ ┌ ┐ └ ┘ ├ ┤ ┬ ┴ ┼`, the edit icon `±`, the mode setting `◆`, a finished run's `✓` |
| `-` | `─ ┄ ┈`, the minus `−` |
| `=` | `━` (context bar fill, scroll and pan thumbs, the prompt rule), the read icon `≡` |
| `\|` | `│ ┆ ▌` |
| `#` | `┃` (the conversation's scroll thumb), a checked `■` |
| `?` | the search icon `◎` |
| `x` | the delete icon `⌫`, a failure `✗` |
| `>` | `➜ › ▸` |
| `$` | the run icon `❯` |
| `v` | `↓ ▾` |
| `^` | `↑` |
| `:` | the think icon `∴` |
| `~` | the mode icon `◇` |
| `*` | `• ▪ ● ✻` |
| `o` | `○` |
| `_` | an unchecked `□` |
| `c` | the copy button `⧉` |
| `.` | `⋯ … ·` |
| spinner frames | `◐ ◓ ◑ ◒`, `◴ ◷ ◶ ◵` and the braille frames each map to one of `\| / - \` in turn |
| `1`–`9`, `A`–`K` | the chips `①`–`⑳` |

Known rough edges. `◐` is both a status-spinner frame and the effort setting's icon, so the effort setting shows `|`. `◷` is both an agent-spinner frame and the "last turn" mark, so that mark shows `/`. A scenario's mouse steps aim at the text on screen, so `scenarios/readme/tour.json`, which clicks `⧉`, plays only in Unicode. The README does not mention the key yet. Its config section is Jack's.
